questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake light.
Less noticeable than a car's brake light.
Less important than a car's brake light.
Easier to see than a car's brake light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake light.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually harder to see than a car's brake light. Flash your brake light before you slow down or stop. This helps other drivers notice you are braking.

questions.question: The best source for information about your motorcycle is:
questions.explanation: Use your owner's manual as your main source for information about your motorcycle. It tells you the motorcycle's details, how to operate it, and what maintenance it needs.

questions.question: You should do a pre-ride inspection:
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This stops mechanical problems from causing danger. Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car.

questions.question: When choosing shoes for riding, pick:
questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are high and sturdy. They should support and cover your ankles. Heels should be short so they don't catch on things. Tuck in any laces so they don't catch on the motorcycle's moving parts.

questions.question: When riding on a bridge grating, you should:

options.text: Always ride on the far right side of the lane.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to weave slightly. This is normal and not dangerous. Just relax and cross at a steady speed. Do not zigzag to fight the weaving—this is dangerous and makes you lose control.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen often, so don't worry about them.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can kill.

questions.question: A face shield:
questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield gives the most protection for your eyes and face. Regular eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough. In Vermont, you do not need eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still recommended.

questions.question: You should wear reflective clothing:
questions.explanation: Always wear reflective and bright-colored clothing when riding. Crashes happen during the day and at night. Wear highly visible clothing at all times.

questions.question: Proper motorcycle riding clothes should:

options.text: Cover your arms but not your legs.
Cover your legs but not your arms.
Be whatever feels comfortable, safety does not matter.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely. This protects you while riding.

questions.question: Motorcycle signals are:

options.text: Even more important than signals on cars or trucks.
Only needed when another vehicle is next to you.
Less important than signals on cars or trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even more important than signals on cars or trucks.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are more at risk than car or truck drivers. Using signals correctly is even more important for motorcyclists than for other drivers.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out and hit you.
Other drivers may drive slowly while looking for a spot.
The road surface may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out and hit you.
questions.explanation: Parked cars are dangerous because drivers may pull out without looking. Car doors may open into your path, and people may step out between cars.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes, slow down, and avoid sudden moves. Watch out for oil, shade, dirt, gravel, and bridges—these surfaces have less grip.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle, which is called engine braking.

questions.question: For best protection, wear a helmet certified by the:
questions.explanation: Buy a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards for maximum protection.

questions.question: How does riding with a passenger affect your motorcycle?

options.text: It makes no difference in how it handles.
It is usually safe for new riders.
It changes how the motorcycle handles.
It helps riders get used to different conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It changes how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight, which changes how your motorcycle handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: One benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance is:

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take very little time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: With proper maintenance and regular inspections, your motorcycle will continue to run like new.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
Ride the same way you do without a passenger.
Make sure footrests are only for you.
Tell the passenger what to do after you start riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must be equipped and adjusted for a passenger. It needs a large enough seat, separate footrests for the passenger, and may need adjustments to headlight, tire pressure, and suspension for the extra weight.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Stay in the same lane position at all times.
Weave across the lane to keep other drivers away.
Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No one lane position is always best. Change your position based on what is happening on the road and with traffic.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you must:

options.text: Complete the pass in a no passing zone.
Start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
Use your horn to make the driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passes must start and end in areas where passing is safe and legal, and within posted speed limits.

questions.question: What is the best source of information about your motorcycle?

options.text: Someone who owns a different type of motorcycle
A television show about motorcycle riding

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. The manual gives you information specific to your bike.

questions.question: Crashes happen most often to which group?

options.text: Riders who know their motorcycle well
Riders who completed a safety course

questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often to new riders who have not been trained and do not know their motorcycle yet.

questions.question: What is the helmet requirement for motorcycle passengers?

options.text: Required only if the driver has had their license for two years or less
Required only if the driver had a traffic ticket in the last two years

questions.explanation: In North Carolina, both riders and passengers must wear helmets on motorcycles. Helmets must meet DOT safety standards.

questions.question: Which surface is NOT slippery?

options.text: Oil stripe in the center of a lane

questions.explanation: Many surfaces are slippery for motorcycles. These include wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, oil, and metal plates. Dry pavement provides good traction for tires.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is located on the right handgrip and is controlled with your right hand.
